primary_meaning: A “name” most commonly symbolizes the identity and revealed character of the person who bears it; in biblical usage it can therefore represent the person himself or herself, including that person’s presence, reputation, and authority. God’s name especially signifies God as revealed and made known.
primary_basis: Exodus 3:13–15 — God’s revealed name is associated with his identity and covenantal self-disclosure.
Exodus 34:5–7 — the LORD proclaims his name by declaring his character and attributes.
Psalm 20:7 — trusting in the name of the LORD means trusting in God himself.
Proverbs 18:10 — the name of the LORD represents God’s protective presence and power.
Matthew 1:21–23 — Jesus’ names identify his mission and significance.
John 17:6, 26 — Jesus makes the Father’s name known, commonly understood as revealing God’s person and character.
Philippians 2:9–11 — the exalted name of Jesus signifies supreme status and authority.

alternatives.meaning: Delegated authority or agency: acting “in the name” of someone means acting under that person’s authorization and power.
Reputation, honor, or renown: a good or great name represents public standing and remembered reputation.
Covenant ownership and belonging: bearing, receiving, or having a name written signifies being claimed by God and included among his people.
A divinely assigned vocation or transformed identity: receiving a new name marks a changed status, mission, or eschatological identity.
Continued existence or memorial: preserving or blotting out a name can symbolize enduring remembrance, lineage, or removal from the community.

notes: There is broad consensus on the core idea of identity or character represented by a name, but no single exclusive symbolic definition applies in every passage. Context determines whether identity, authority, reputation, belonging, or vocation is emphasized.
